output.summary: Approved G1040 design revision 2 (review round 2 approved, no open findings). Findings on a blocked node reach its retry card: a blocked agent record keeps the replaced output (last_output) behind capability blocked_findings, and frontier pass 1 treats a consumer stale only because of the block as fresh (no stale_review, op findings kept, nothing carried). The rollout policy PR that requires blocked_findings must ship G1026's revised design.md step 4 (enforced by a repository test). The 'arrived while you ran' refusal becomes per-id reasons; a run_tests failure is a repeat only when its normalised text matches (0x/hex/tempfile names normalised).

responses.review_design:1:1: fixed: took the reviewer's rule and made it exact. The blocked record now stores last_output (the replaced done output, copied across a second block) rather than last_out_fp, because a consumer's fp_parts hold selected values that cannot be recomputed from an output fingerprint, so 'stale only because of the block' could not be proven for a consumer that saw an older output of the held node, or for a filter. Pass 1 alone uses a held view: recorded(p), the subject check/fp_parts and liveness read the held output (§3.1). Such consumers are fresh, so they are not in res.stale: (a) op carriers' findings on a held target are kept (new test 13: run_tests:failed on a blocked implement reaches the retry card); (b) no stale_review and no 'made it moot' text (test 2 asserts both, and that review_design and filter_design are not stale); (c) carried_findings is empty for an edit no consumer reads (new test 4b). A consumer whose own inputs changed stays stale and carried: G1026's spec-edit case is genuinely stale (review_design reads goal.spec), so test 4 asserts stale_review true and the carried_findings entry rather than their absence, as G1028 intends. New test 5b pins that a consumer that saw an older output stays stale. SPEC §4.9 states the held-view rule. Pass 2 is unchanged.
responses.review_design:1:2: fixed: §3.4 now says the rollout policy PR carries both the requires entry and the revised step 4 in .zzzops/prompts/design.md (the prompt may land earlier, since the new text is right with the capability off; requires never lands before it), with the reason. G1026's text is only in the template, which this goal edits; the installed copy changes only in that policy PR. blocked_findings.txt, SPEC §4.5 and CLI_USAGE say the capability needs the revised design step 4 (doc needle in test 12), and new repository test 14 fails when .zzzops requires blocked_findings and the installed design prompt lacks the needle 'that no entry in `human_decisions` answers', so CI fails a requires-only policy PR. The engine does not gate on prompt text, since prompts are repository-owned free text.
responses.review_design:1:3: fixed: norm now replaces, in order, 0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+ (object addresses), tmp[a-z0-9_]{8} (default tempfile names), (?<=-)[a-z0-9_]{8}(?=[/.]) (the hyphen-ended prefixes this repository's tests use with mkdtemp/mkstemp), [0-9a-f]{7,} without word boundaries, and \d+ (§3.5, SPEC §4.14). Test 9's recurring failure now differs in a timing, commit id, 0x address and both tempfile forms and must give round 2; a norm unit test pins each token kind and that different test names stay different. §6 no longer claims such tokens are rare and names what is still not covered (letter-bearing UUID groups, random words), bounded by the correction budget.

output.summary: Revision 2 of the G1040 design, fixing the three review_design corrections only. (1) Blocked agent records keep the replaced output (last_output, capability blocked_findings) instead of only its fingerprint; pass 1 alone reads held outputs for carriers' inputs, subjects and liveness, so a consumer stale only because of the block is fresh for that node: not in stale, op findings (run_tests/integrate on a blocked implement) kept, no stale_review, no carried_findings; genuinely stale consumers (spec edit) keep G1028's carry. (2) The rollout policy PR ships the revised design step 4 with the requires entry (prompt may land first, requires never before); capability text, SPEC 4.5 and CLI_USAGE say so; a repository test pins the pairing. (3) norm also replaces 0x addresses, unbounded hex runs of 7+, and default and hyphen-prefixed tempfile names; test 9 and a norm unit test cover them.

findings.text: Every carrier of a blocked target's findings is a stale carrier (pass 1: fresh[c] is False when its subject or input is the blocked node, because the subject is not done and resolve(recorded) gives Missing), so §3.1's 'carrier rules apply as today' sends the findings through G1028's carry branch. Impact: (a) op carriers are never carried, so run_tests/integrate findings on a blocked implement are still dropped from its retry card, against outcome 2 and the spec, and the design does not say so. (b) Every retry correction gets stale_review: true, and output_schema invites 'disputed: … if the change made it moot' on a retry where nothing changed, which can raise rounds on owner questions and ordinary findings until they escalate. (c) Any edit while the target is blocked lists them in carried_findings with waive lines. Fix: a carrier that is not fresh only because a blocked agent target with last_out_fp hides its output counts as unchanged for that target (not in `stale`, and an op carrier's finding is kept). Otherwise state and pin each exclusion in SPEC §4.9 and §8. Add 'no stale_review' and 'no carried_findings' assertions to tests 2 and 4, and a test for an op finding on a blocked implement.

Rollout: G1026 puts its step-4 text only in the template prompt, and installed prompts change through a policy PR. That text says that when a correction starts 'owner question:' the designer must not decide it and must submit --blocked. With blocked_findings required, the answered question is a correction on the retry card, so the designer re-blocks after every answer, and each retry needs another human answer. §3.4's rollout adds only the requires entry, and 'wherever G1026 put its text' leaves the repository prompt open. Fix: the policy PR that requires blocked_findings also carries the new step-4 text (same change, or after it). Say in blocked_findings.txt and in CLI_USAGE or MIGRATING that the capability needs the revised step 4, and pin the pairing with a doc needle.

norm (\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b|\d+) misses tokens that vary between runs of one failure. In CPython object addresses (0x7f3a9c0d1e20) there is no word boundary after 'x', so the hex letters remain and differ. Tempfile names (/tmp/tmpk3j_9x2a) are random letters. This repository's git- and tempdir-based test output prints both, so §6's 'rarely print' does not hold. Impact (moderate, bounded by the budget): a real repeat compares as new, gets round 1, never escalates, and implement loops until the correction budget. Fix: also replace 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+ and tmp[a-z0-9_]{8} (or any run of 7 or more hex characters, without \b), state it in SPEC §4.14, and add both cases to test 9.

output.summary: Revision 2 fixes all three round-1 findings. 1:1: the held view in pass 1 (recorded inputs, subject and fp_parts, liveness) is exact against frontier.py at 25186a5. A consumer that is stale only because of the block is fresh, so it is not in res.stale: no stale_review, no carried_findings, op findings kept, filter still fresh. Test 4's stale_review: true is right, because review_design, adversary_design and filter_design all read goal.spec. last_output does not grow the goal doc (it replaces the done record's output, and output becomes null) and never reaches a card. 1:2: one policy PR or prompt first, documented, with test 14 run by validate.yml on every PR; G1026's frozen needles survive the new sentences. 1:3: norm's alternation order and anchors cover 0x addresses, hex runs, tmpXXXXXXXX and every hyphen-prefixed tempfile name in the repository. Three non-blocking notes are in the artifact: quoted-path lookahead, the test 4b example field, and keeping the carrier guard on R.

spec:
Found while dogfooding Release 1 (dogfood notes 62, 73, 74, 75). A finding is live only while its target's latest record is done and current, so:
- After a node blocks (an owner question) or goes stale (an input changed), its re-run card shows `corrections: []` although findings against it are still open; answering them is refused with "no live finding ... Findings arrived while you ran", which is wrong. The root relayed findings to workers by hand several times.
- A second, different run_tests failure reuses the id `run_tests:failed` and is treated as a repeat, raising a needs_human dispute that says implement answered '' although it had answered "fixed: ...".

Owner decision (verbatim): "3. Ok" (to carrying open findings onto the re-run's card and accepting answers to them), and "I think we may as well get these done now, before dogfooding again".

Scope:
- A re-run card of a stale or blocked node lists the open findings against that node as corrections, and submit accepts responses to them.
- A refusal for a finding that is no longer live says why (resolved, superseded, target changed) and to drop it, instead of "arrived while you ran".
- A new run_tests failure with different text is a new round, not a repeat; a dispute question shows the target's actual last response.
- Check this against G1026's option (b) (owner questions resolved by the re-review) and keep that flow working.

Acceptance:
- Replays of the G1026 cases (review_tests findings on test_design, then a design change staling test_design) show the findings on the stale card and accept fixed: responses.
- Two different run_tests failures in a row give two rounds and no dispute.
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes and adds a HISTORY §4 row.
title: Carry open findings onto stale and blocked re-run cards
